evidence: X-ray diffraction (XRD) results shown in Fig. 1(a) revealed that the as-deposited sample has a very broad feature around 32°, representing amorphous material and a very dim (222) peak, indicating the presence of a limited number of small crystals. Cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) on a fully crystallized sample has revealed a large grain size and an excellent grain crystal quality. Atomic force microscopy revealed a negligible RMS roughness of the films (<0.6 nm), both before and after crystallization. The absorption coefficient has been extracted from spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) data. The electronic properties as a function of film crystallinity, as obtained from Hall measurements, is shown in Fig. 3. Elastic recoil detection (ERD) analysis was used to determine the H content of the as-deposited samples.
